premise.usage: Node kind: a thesis that rests on nothing else. One or two words. Also used lowercased in the legend.

conclusion.usage: Node kind: a thesis derived from others. One or two words. Also used lowercased in the legend.

restsOn.usage: Heading above the list of a thesis's premises. Up to three words, shown in capitals.

leadsTo.usage: Heading above the list of what follows from a thesis. Up to three words, shown in capitals.

derived.usage: Line above a conclusion's text; {refs} becomes a list of clickable numbers joined with the language's own 'and'.

noPremises.en: A starting premise: it rests on nothing else in the chain.
noPremises.usage: Shown instead of the premises list for a premise. One sentence.

noConsequences.en: A final conclusion: nothing follows from it.
noConsequences.usage: Shown instead of the consequences list for a final conclusion. One sentence.

prev.usage: Button: go to the previous thesis in reading order. Keep the arrow.

next.usage: Button: go to the next thesis in reading order. Keep the arrow.

collapse.usage: Button that collapses the side panel. One word.

expand.usage: Button that expands the collapsed side panel. One word.

fitAll.usage: Button that fits the whole graph on screen. Two words at most.

legendSelected.usage: Legend item for the selected node. Shown lowercased.

legendAncestors.usage: Legend item for nodes the selected one depends on, directly or indirectly. Shown lowercased.

legendDescendants.usage: Legend item for nodes that follow from the selected one. Shown lowercased.

hint.en: Drag or scroll to move the graph; Ctrl + scroll or + and − zoom. ← → go in order, ↑ to a premise, ↓ to a consequence, 0 shows the whole graph.
hint.usage: Help line at the bottom of the panel. Keep the key names as they appear on a keyboard.

graphLabel.en: Thesis graph: arrows lead from premises to conclusions
graphLabel.usage: Accessible label of the whole graph for screen readers.

nodeLabel.usage: Accessible label of a node for screen readers.

source.usage: Label before the link to the original article in the header. One word.

error.usage: Shown instead of the graph when the data is invalid. {message} is a technical English message.

glossary.meaning: A starting claim the reasoning rests on
A claim derived from other claims
Any single claim in the graph, premise or conclusion
A claim that follows from the selected one
